# Story 01 — Ticket Management operational features (bulk, links, merge, watchers, tags, saved views, category admin, manual escalation)

## Prerequisites

- None. This extends already-shipped ticketing code (see intake "Already shipped by the bootstrap"). Coordinate with the owners of `sla-automation` (they consume the new **watchers** and **escalation** signals) and `channels` (they invoke the new **merge** endpoint from inbound-mail threading).
- Read the existing tickets area end-to-end before touching anything — the intake explicitly forbids duplicating the workflow rules or bypassing `TicketWorkflow`.

---

## Story Goal

Turn the shipped single-ticket lifecycle into a support-desk-grade workflow. Deliver, in one coordinated slice:

1. **Bulk actions** (assign / priority / status) from `TicketListView`, with per-item success/failure reporting.
2. **Typed ticket-to-ticket links** (`DuplicateOf`, `RelatedTo`, `Blocks`) rendered on both endpoints.
3. **Ticket merge** — comments, attachments and interactions rehomed onto the target; source auto-closed with a history entry naming the target.
4. **Watchers** (self and colleagues) exposed on the ticket detail and via API so `sla-automation` can notify them.
5. **Free-form tags** with list-page filter.
6. **Personal saved views** (named filter combinations) persisted per Identity user.
7. **Admin/Manager-managed category tree** — create/rename/reorder/reparent/deactivate. Deactivation hides from pickers but leaves existing tickets untouched.
8. **Manual escalation level** raise/lower with a mandatory reason in history.
9. **Ticket history** records every one of the above mutations.

Out of scope: automatic escalation rules (`sla-automation`), AI auto-categorisation (`ai-features`), inbound e-mail/WhatsApp ticket creation (`channels`).

Cross-cutting constraints from the intake (Arabic-default full RTL, 375px responsive, department/branch scoping, soft delete + audit trail, no weakening of `options.FallbackPolicy`, `dotnet test` + `npm run build` green) apply to every change below.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** single-ticket assign / status / comment / history via `TicketService` + `TicketsController`. Categories exposed read-only through `LookupsController`. No tags, watchers, links, merge, bulk, saved views, manual escalation-level.
- **New behaviour:** all of the above, added additively. **No** existing endpoint changes signature; new columns are nullable; `TicketDto`/`TicketDetailDto` may grow optional fields (`Tags`, `Watchers`, `Links`, `EscalationLevel`) but existing fields stay put so shipped clients keep working.

### 4 — Application services

#### 4a — Extend `TicketService` and `ITicketService`

Add methods, each returning `Task` and taking `CancellationToken`:

- `BulkAssignAsync(BulkAssignRequest req, ...)`, `BulkChangePriorityAsync(...)`, `BulkChangeStatusAsync(...)` — implement as a **loop over the existing single-ticket methods** (`AssignAsync`, `UpdateAsync` or a new small `ChangePriorityAsync`, and `ChangeStatusAsync`). Catch `AppException` per item, translate to `BulkItemResult(Succeeded=false, ErrorCode=ex.GetType().Name, ErrorMessage=ex.Message)`. Never wrap the loop in a single transaction — successes must persist even when other items fail. Write one `TicketHistory` row per successful item using the existing history helpers, and one aggregate log per bulk call is **not** required (per-item history satisfies the audit criterion).
- `AddLinkAsync(sourceId, CreateTicketLinkRequest)` — reject self-link, reject duplicate `(source,target,type)`, verify both tickets are in the caller's scope via `IScopeProvider`. Insert row; write `LinkAdded` to both tickets' history (record the reciprocal on the target so the intake criterion "the links render on both detail pages" is trivially satisfied by loading `OutgoingLinks ∪ IncomingLinks`).
- `RemoveLinkAsync(sourceId, linkId)` — soft delete; history on both sides.
- `MergeAsync(sourceId, MergeTicketRequest)`:
  1. Load both tickets; both must be in scope; source must not already be closed/merged.
  2. Reassign `TicketComment.TicketId`, `Interaction.TicketId`, and `Attachment` rows whose `OwnerType == AttachmentOwnerType.Ticket && OwnerId == sourceId` to point at the target (bulk `UpdateAsync`-style through EF).
  3. Move watchers/tags/links (dedupe against target).
  4. Append a `TicketComment` on the target (internal note) saying "Merged from #{sourceReference}" — bilingual key.
  5. Set source status to `Closed` **through `TicketWorkflow`** with reason "Merged into #{targetReference}"; if the workflow disallows it from the current state, force via a dedicated `CloseAsMergedAsync` helper that bypasses `TicketWorkflow` **only** for merges, and record the reason in history so the exception is auditable.
  6. Write `Merged` history on source and `MergedInto` on target.
  7. Persist. Return updated target detail.
- `AddWatcherAsync` / `RemoveWatcherAsync` — self or (for Supervisory+) colleague; validate the user exists via `IIdentityService`.
- `AddTagAsync` / `RemoveTagAsync` — resolve or create `Tag` by case-insensitive `Name`; upsert `TicketTag`; write history.
- `RaiseEscalationAsync` / `LowerEscalationAsync` — mutate `Ticket.EscalationLevel` (`null`/`0` floor; cap at a sane max like `5`); require reason; write history `EscalationRaised`/`EscalationLowered` including `FromValue`/`ToValue`.

Extend `SearchAsync` (or its query DTO) with optional `IReadOnlyList<Guid>? TagIds` filter — apply via `.Where(t => t.TicketTags.Any(x => tagIds.Contains(x.TagId)))`. Keep the existing filters intact.

Extend the detail projection to populate `Tags`, `Watchers`, `Links` (union of outgoing+incoming, mapped so `TargetTicketId` on the DTO is always the "other" ticket from the caller's viewpoint), and `EscalationLevel`.

**Do not touch `AllowedNextStatuses`** — it stays driven by `TicketWorkflow.AllowedTransitions`.

Inject `IClock` for any timestamp; never call `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` directly.

Register in `Application/DependencyInjection.cs`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Bulk with mixed permissions / scope:** items outside the caller's department/branch fail with `ForbiddenException` and appear as failed rows; enforced in the service by re-using `TicketService.AssignAsync`/`ChangeStatusAsync` which already run through `IScopeProvider`.
- **Bulk status with illegal transition:** the per-item call throws from `TicketWorkflow.ValidateTransition`; captured as `BulkItemResult(Succeeded=false, ErrorCode="ConflictException", ...)`; the loop continues. Verified in `TicketWorkflow.cs`.
- **Bulk cap:** more than 200 ticket ids in one request is rejected by `BulkAssignRequestValidator` etc. with `BadRequestException`.
- **Merge into self:** `MergeTicketRequestValidator` rejects `TargetTicketId == sourceId`.
- **Merge with target in different department/branch:** rejected by scope check in `MergeAsync`; `ForbiddenException`.
- **Merge chain (A→B, then B→C):** `MergeAsync` refuses when source is already `Closed`; the source of a prior merge stays closed and its links are preserved. Document this limitation in code comments so `channels` sees it.
- **Duplicate link add:** unique index `(SourceTicketId, TargetTicketId, Type)` throws `DbUpdateException`; service pre-checks and throws `ConflictException` with a friendlier message.
- **Reciprocal link render:** the detail projection unions `OutgoingLinks` and `IncomingLinks`; for incoming, the DTO swaps source/target so the frontend always sees "this ticket → other".
- **Category cycle:** `TicketCategoryService.UpdateAsync` walks ancestors and throws `BadRequestException` when a cycle is detected.
- **Deactivating a category still in use:** allowed; existing tickets keep their `CategoryId`. Pickers (`LookupsController` category tree) filter out `IsActive=false` **only from the picker projection**; the ticket-detail read must still resolve inactive categories by id so the label renders.
- **Deleting a category still referenced by open tickets:** rejected with `ConflictException`.
- **Watcher = deleted / disabled Identity user:** watcher list projection tolerates missing users by falling back to `UserId` as the display name; do not throw.
- **Tag name collisions (case, whitespace, unicode):** the service normalises with `Trim()` + `ToUpperInvariant()` for comparison but stores the original casing; unique index enforced on the normalised form. Arabic tag names (e.g. `عاجل`) must round-trip; add a test with an Arabic-only tag.
- **Saved view `FiltersJson` malformed:** validator parses with `JsonDocument.Parse`; throws `BadRequestException` on failure.
- **Saved view size:** hard cap 8 KB per view; 200 views per user per `EntityKind` (enforce in `UpsertAsync`).
- **Escalation level below 0 / above cap:** service clamps and throws `BadRequestException` when the requested delta would exceed bounds.
- **Concurrent bulk on the same ticket:** two agents bulk-assigning the same ticket both succeed; the second overwrites the first; last-writer-wins is acceptable because the audit trail records both actions.
- **RTL numeric layout:** ticket ids inside the bulk-result list must be wrapped `class="ltr-nums"`; verify visually in Arabic.
- **375px viewport:** the bulk toolbar collapses to a `⋯` menu; the links/watchers/tags sections stack vertically.
- **Fallback auth policy:** all new endpoints inherit `[Authorize]`; none use `[AllowAnonymous]`. Confirm via `grep AllowAnonymous` after adding controllers — should return only pre-existing hits.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration name: `TicketOpsFeatures`. All new columns on `Ticket` are **nullable**; all new tables are additive. Safe to deploy to a live database.
- Rollback: `dotnet ef migrations remove` before deploy; if already applied, generate an inverse migration that drops the new tables and the `EscalationLevel` column. Because all changes are additive, a partially applied state (schema present, code rolled back) leaves the system fully functional — the new columns/tables are simply ignored.
- Data migration: none required. Existing tickets have `EscalationLevel = null`, empty `Tags`, `Watchers`, `Links`.
- If deploy fails after the migration but before code rollout, the API is still healthy because none of the new columns are `NOT NULL`.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx`
2. **Backend tests:** `dotnet test backend/CustomerSupportCRM.slnx` — expect all pre-existing 72 tests plus the new ones to pass.
3. **Apply migration to dev DB:**
   `dotnet ef database update --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Infrastructure --startup-project backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api`
4. **Frontend builds:** `npm run build --prefix frontend`
5. **Frontend dev:** `npm run dev --prefix frontend` and manually exercise, in **Arabic (default)** and English:
   - Bulk assign / priority / status on 3 tickets where one is deliberately in a status that forbids the target transition; verify per-item error message.
   - Create a `DuplicateOf` link between two tickets; open the other one and confirm the reciprocal link appears.
   - Merge ticket A into B; confirm A is closed with a history line naming B, and B has A's comments/attachments/interactions.
   - Add self and a colleague as watchers; remove both.
   - Add tags including one Arabic-only tag (`عاجل`) and one with mixed casing; filter list by tag.
   - Save a filter combination as a personal view, navigate away, come back, re-select — same rows appear.
   - As an Admin/Manager, open `/admin/ticket-categories`, create/rename/reparent/reorder/deactivate; confirm ticket-new-form picker hides deactivated categories but existing tickets still show the label.
   - Raise then lower escalation level; verify the reason appears in history and that submitting an empty reason is blocked.
6. **RTL / 375px:** switch to Arabic and Chrome dev-tools 375px width; verify list, detail and Category admin pages have no clipped controls and digits render LTR inside Arabic labels.
7. **Regression:** ticket search + status buttons (`AllowedNextStatuses`) still render exactly as before; existing `TicketServiceTests` unchanged and green.
8. **Auth:** `grep -n "AllowAnonymous" backend/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Api` returns only the pre-existing hits — no new anonymous endpoints.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] Bulk assign / priority / status endpoints exist, reuse the single-ticket services, and surface per-item results; per-item failure does not roll back the batch.
- [ ] `TicketLink` with `DuplicateOf` / `RelatedTo` / `Blocks` is persisted, unique per `(source,target,type)`, and rendered on both endpoints.
- [ ] `MergeAsync` reassigns comments, attachments, interactions to the target, closes the source with a history line naming the target, and the customer thread on the target contains the merged content.
- [ ] Watchers can be added/removed (self + colleague) and are exposed on `TicketDetailDto.Watchers` for `sla-automation` to consume.
- [ ] Free-form `Tag`s can be added/removed on a ticket; `SearchAsync` accepts `tagIds` and the list page filters by tag.
- [ ] Personal `UserSavedView`s persist per Identity user, keyed by `EntityKind="Ticket"`; the list page can save, re-select, and delete them.
- [ ] `TicketCategoriesController` supports create / rename / reorder / reparent / deactivate; deactivation hides from pickers but preserves existing ticket labels; delete is refused when open tickets reference the category.
- [ ] `Ticket.EscalationLevel` can be raised and lowered by 1 with a **mandatory reason**; both changes appear in ticket history.
- [ ] Every new mutation writes a `TicketHistory` row (or `AuditLog` for category admin) with a stable `Action` string.
- [ ] All new DTOs mirrored in `frontend/src/types/api.ts`; all new user-visible strings present in both `ar.json` and `en.json`; `locales.spec.ts` passes.
- [ ] Every screen usable at 375px in RTL; ticket numbers wrapped `ltr-nums`.
- [ ] `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, `npm run build` all succeed.
- [ ] No new `[AllowAnonymous]` endpoints; category admin restricted to Admin/Manager.
- [ ] Migration `TicketOpsFeatures` is additive and reversible; no changes to existing columns.
